title: Edward Dyer opens a brewery at Kasauli
body: Edward Dyer travelled from England to the Himalayan hill station of Kasauli, drawn by spring water and a climate that reminded him of Scotland, and set up what is generally described as India's first brewery. Sources differ on the exact year, some placing it in the late 1820s, others in 1830, so this date should be read as approximate.
source_title: Wikipedia, Kasauli Brewery and Distillery

title: The Kasauli operation is incorporated as Dyer Breweries
body: Edward Dyer's brewery was formally incorporated as Dyer Breweries, later Edward Dyer and Co Ltd. Production eventually moved to Solan, and the original Kasauli site was converted into a distillery.
source_title: Wikipedia, Kasauli Brewery and Distillery

title: H G Meakin buys the Shimla and Solan breweries
body: H G Meakin moved to India and set up Meakin and Co Ltd, then bought the old Shimla and Solan breweries from Edward Dyer. This purchase is the direct line to the company that later became Mohan Meakin.
source_title: Wikipedia, Mohan Meakin

title: N N Mohan buys the Dyer Meakin assets
body: After independence, Narendra Nath Mohan bought a majority stake in Dyer Meakin Breweries and acquired its Indian assets. The company was renamed Mohan Meakin in 1967 and remains the direct descendant of the Kasauli brewery.
source_title: Wikipedia, Kasauli Brewery and Distillery

title: Vijay Mallya relaunches Kingfisher
body: Vijay Mallya rebranded United Breweries' beer as Kingfisher to compete with Mohan Meakin's Golden Eagle. Kingfisher went on to take over a third of the Indian beer market, setting the mass market lager baseline that craft brewing would later react against.
source_title: Wikipedia, Kingfisher (beer)

title: Howzatt opens at Gurgaon's Galaxy Hotel
body: Howzatt, a cricket themed brewpub at the Galaxy Hotel and Spa in Gurgaon, is described by several trade sources as India's first commercial microbrewery, with brewing equipment supplied by Rohit Jafa Brewing Solutions. This claim sits alongside, and sometimes in tension with, the more widely repeated story that credits Pune's Doolally as the first.
source_title: Rohit Jafa Brewing Solutions, Microbrewery India

title: Doolally opens in Pune
body: Doolally opened at The Corinthians hotel in Pune, founded by Oliver Schauf and Suketu Talekar, and is the brewpub most commonly cited in the press as India's first microbrewery. Talekar had approached Maharashtra's excise department in 2007, and it took roughly two and a half years to get the law amended before the brewery could open, which is why some accounts still give Howzatt in Gurgaon the earlier claim.
source_title: Wikipedia, Beer in India

title: Karnataka becomes the first state with formal microbrewery excise rules
body: Karnataka amended the Karnataka Brewery Rules, 1967 to allow bars, hotels and clubs to open microbreweries, making it the first Indian state to write a clear rulebook for the format. That early clarity is a large part of why Bengaluru went on to have more microbreweries than any other Indian city.
source_title: Rohit Jafa Brewing Solutions, state wise microbrewery policy, Karnataka

title: Toit opens in Indiranagar
body: Three friends, Sibi Venkataraju, Arun George and Mukesh Tolani, opened Toit in Bengaluru's Indiranagar neighbourhood after working through the licensing hurdles that Karnataka's new rules had just opened up. Toit became one of the best known brewpub names in the country and later grew into a small chain.
source_title: YourStory, Toit Story

title: Gateway Brewing Co founded in Mumbai
body: Navin Mittal, known online as the IndianBeerGeek, founded Gateway Brewing Co with Krishna Naik and Rahul Mehra as one of Mumbai's first microbreweries. It commercially launched its taproom in 2014 and went on to open a retail store near the Gateway of India.
source_title: Hospibuz, Gateway Brewing Co celebrates 8 years

title: Independence Brewing Company founded in Pune
body: Shailendra Bist founded Independence Brewing Company in Pune, which grew into one of the city's landmark craft beer destinations and later expanded to Mumbai.
source_title: Tracxn, Independence Brewing Company company profile

title: Arbor Brewing Company opens Bengaluru's first American style brewpub
body: Matt Greff, who had helped pioneer American craft brewing in Ann Arbor, Michigan in the 1990s, partnered with Bengaluru native Gaurav Sikka to bring Arbor Brewing Company to India. It opened as the first American style brewpub in the country and later added a Goa location.
source_title: Arbor Brewing Company India

title: White Owl Brewery starts life as a restaurant in Mumbai
body: Javed Murad opened White Owl as a restaurant in Mumbai's Lower Parel in 2013, then converted it into a brewery in 2014 once the licences came through. It later expanded into bottled and canned distribution across several cities.
source_title: YourStory, White Owl Brewery

title: Bira 91 launches
body: Ankur Jain, who had spent years importing European and American craft beer into India, launched Bira 91 through his company B9 Beverages in early 2015. It became the most recognisable Indian craft beer brand, later opening production in Madhya Pradesh and Nagpur and raising funding from Sequoia, Sofina and Kirin Holdings.
source_title: Wikipedia, Bira 91

title: Telangana notifies its Micro Brewery Rules
body: Telangana's excise department issued the Telangana Micro Brewery Rules, 2015 and invited applications, positioning Hyderabad alongside Bengaluru, Mumbai, Pune and Gurugram as a microbrewery city. Around 60 applications had come in within a year.
source_title: ILEP Federation, Telangana Micro Brewery Rules 2015

title: Simba launches out of Chhattisgarh
body: Simba launched with its own brewery in Durg, Chhattisgarh, an unusual base for an Indian craft beer brand, and grew quickly through bottled and canned distribution.
source_title: YourStory, Simba Brewery

title: White Rhino becomes the first Indian craft beer brewed and bottled in India
body: Ishaan Puri founded White Rhino at Malanpur, near Gwalior, on a tributary of the Chambal river chosen for its brewing water. Reporting from the time describes it as the first Indian craft beer to be both brewed and bottled domestically, launching with a lager and a Belgian style wit.
source_title: Wikipedia, White Rhino (brewery)

title: Pune hosts India's first craft beer competition
body: Independence Brewing Company organised the Independence Craft Beer Invitational in Pune on 27 and 28 May 2017. Seventy six beers across nine categories were entered from breweries in Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru, Haryana and Kolkata, judged by a panel of seven professional brewers.
source_title: Gigglewater, India's First Craft Beer Competition

title: White Rhino starts exporting to the United Kingdom
body: White Rhino partnered with West Yorkshire based distributor James Clay to export its lager and India pale ale to Britain, an early sign that Indian craft beer could travel beyond the domestic market.
source_title: Wikipedia, White Rhino (brewery)

title: Kati Patang launches, brewed across the Bhutan border
body: Lata and Shantanu Upadhyay launched Kati Patang in October 2018, brewing the beer in Bhutan with water drawn from the upper Himalayas before selling it into the Indian market, a distinctive supply chain among Indian craft brands.
source_title: Business Today, Brewed To Taste

title: Brewocrat runs the first Weizenbier Fest in Gurgaon
body: Brewocrat hosted the Weizenbier Fest in Gurgaon in 2019, billed as the first festival of its kind in India dedicated to fresh, hand crafted wheat beer, adding to a growing calendar of dedicated craft beer events beyond the big multi brewery festivals.
source_title: LBB Delhi, First of its kind handcrafted brew fest in Gurgaon

title: India passes two hundred brewpubs
body: By 2019, India had more than two hundred brewpubs, a scale that would have been unimaginable a decade earlier when Doolally and Howzatt were the only names in the country.
source_title: Wikipedia, Beer in India

title: Lockdown forces breweries to drain their tanks
body: When the 2020 lockdown shut brewpubs across the country, breweries had to drain unsold beer that was ageing in tanks and eating electricity for nothing. Gateway Brewing Company in Mumbai alone reported draining somewhere between 50,000 and 100,000 litres, one of many craft breweries fighting to survive the shutdown.
source_title: Business Today, Brewing Trouble

title: Maharashtra allows growler takeaway as a lockdown revenue measure
body: To give shuttered microbreweries some income during the lockdown, Maharashtra's excise department allowed them to sell fresh beer for takeaway in growlers on an experimental basis. The state later made this policy permanent, becoming the first in India to do so.
source_title: Brewer World, Maharashtra's permanent growler policy

title: Bira 91 holds volumes while the wider industry shrinks
body: Through the financial year to March 2021, Bira 91's sales volumes stayed roughly level with the year before even as the overall beer market contracted, and its market share doubled compared with the prior year, a sign that the craft segment recovered faster than the mass market.
source_title: YourStory, How Indian craft beer brands survived COVID-19

title: Delhi's new excise policy lets microbreweries sell growlers for the first time
body: Delhi's Excise Policy for 2021-22, published on 5 July 2021, finally let microbreweries sell draught beer for takeaway in bottles or growlers and supply draught beer to other licensed bars and restaurants, catching up with a practice already common just across the border in Gurugram.
source_title: The Tribune, Delhi's new excise policy to promote microbreweries

title: Delhi's liberal excise policy is scrapped, and old restrictions return
body: The 2021-22 excise policy that had briefly freed up Delhi's microbreweries was withdrawn amid allegations of irregularities. Owners reported being pushed back to on-premises only sale, no bottling or kegging, and daily output caps of 500 to 1,000 litres, leaving Delhi with only a handful of microbreweries compared with the much larger scene in nearby Gurugram.
source_title: ThePrint, What's holding back Delhi's microbrewery scene

title: United Breweries, AB InBev and Carlsberg form the Brewers Association of India
body: India's three largest beer makers, who together hold around 85 percent of beer sales, launched the Brewers Association of India in Delhi, backed by the World Brewing Alliance and headed by Vinod Giri. This is a mass market industry body, not a craft one, but it changed the lobbying landscape that craft brewers also operate in.
source_title: The Week, Top beer companies launch Brewers Association of India

title: Karnataka updates its brewery rules again
body: Karnataka issued the Karnataka Excise (Brewery) (Amendment) Rules, 2024 on 16 August 2024, revising microbrewery licence fees to two lakh rupees a year, the latest in a long run of amendments to the 1967 rules the state first adapted for microbreweries back in 2010.
source_title: Legality Simplified, New Karnataka Excise (Brewery) (Amendment) Rules 2024

title: Bira 91 runs its Free Flow Festival
body: Bira 91 held its Free Flow Festival at its taproom in October 2024, described by trade press as the largest beer celebration India had seen, a high point that came just before the brand ran into serious financial trouble.
source_title: Brewer World, Free Flow Fest at Bira 91 Taproom

title: Bira 91 halts production and falls into financial crisis
body: Reporting through 2025 shows Bira 91's production coming to a standstill from around July, with founder Ankur Jain describing it as a pause and blaming excise licensing delays after the company's conversion to a public limited entity. Employees say reimbursements went unpaid from November 2024 and salaries fell six months behind, while the company's financial year 2024 results showed a net loss of 748 crore rupees on 638 crore rupees of revenue.
source_title: Storyboard18, The downward spiral of Bira 91

title: Bira 91 staff petition investors as a rescue deal collapses
body: More than 250 Bira 91 employees wrote to the board and investors, including Kirin Holdings and Peak XV Partners, demanding Ankur Jain's removal over unpaid salaries and governance failures. A reported 500 crore rupee investment from BlackRock fell through, and the company instead raised 100 crore rupees through a rights issue priced at a fraction of its earlier valuation.
source_title: Storyboard18, The downward spiral of Bira 91

title: The Great India Beer Fest keeps returning to Delhi
body: The Great India Beer Fest, one of the country's longest running multi brewery festivals, is listed with a September 2026 edition in Delhi, evidence that the festival circuit that grew up alongside the craft scene has kept going even through the industry's harder years.
source_title: District.in, Great India Beer Fest listing
